gen-gf-revalia-gf-noto-sans-grantha: Revalia swaggers in with an open-tailed g and widely spaced letters. Noto Sans Grantha keeps its tall, pressed-flat bowls open, so paragraphs glide along without a single snag from line to line.
gen-gf-revalia-gf-noto-sans-gujarati: Bold, loose swagger: Revalia sprawls its widely spaced letters across the line. Noto Sans Gujarati wins on large open counters, with curved strokes that stop short before turning inward.
gen-gf-revalia-gf-noto-sans-gunjala-gond: Noto Sans Gunjala Gondi writes with chunky, crayon-tall lowercase and terminals cut back to leave a generous gap. Revalia is the loud showpiece; the sans does the quiet work.
gen-gf-revalia-gf-noto-sans-gurmukhi: Noto Sans Gurmukhi reads crisply, its terminals flaring outward like tongs and its ascenders barely clearing the x-height. Revalia grabs attention, then the sans-serif body carries pages along without fuss.
gen-gf-revalia-gf-noto-sans-hanunoo: Noto Sans Hanunoo reads openly, its lowercase filling most of the height and its terminals left easy to follow. And Revalia leans in above with its spaced-out swagger, giving the sans something to push against.
gen-gf-revalia-gf-noto-sans-hebrew: Noto Sans Hebrew lets a dominant midsection swallow the line's height, leaving wide gaps between curve ends and stems. Revalia does the shouting; the plain sans does the explaining.
gen-gf-revalia-gf-noto-sans-hk: Noto Sans HK packs large lowercase forms and tight ascender clearance beneath the loose, wide-striding Revalia. Noto Sans HK stands out for brush ends that lift away before each curve closes.
gen-gf-revalia-gf-noto-sans-imperial-ara: Revalia is the showy one, with an open-tailed g and a relaxed stride. Noto Sans Imperial Aramaic handles the quieter job, its c's ends pointing apart like open pincers.
gen-gf-revalia-gf-noto-sans-inscriptiona: Clean and open, Noto Sans Inscriptional Parthian gives every e and a a big eye and a deep middle band. Revalia shouts, while the plain sans wins on that deep middle band.
gen-gf-revalia-gf-noto-sans-jp: An open-tailed lowercase g gives Revalia its swagger, along with a relaxed stride across widely separated letters. Then Noto Sans JP takes over with a very tall x-height and open sweeping curves that carry text smoothly.
